title: Service Contracts & Acceptance Matrix for Hosted Generation Endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
overview: This PRD defines the service-level contracts, behavioral expectations, and a detailed acceptance matrix for the hosted generation endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). It captures input/output schemas, error semantics, performance SLOs, rollout criteria, and the launch readiness checklist required for GA. The goal is a single, unambiguous source of truth teams can use to implement, test, and validate compatibility between runtime, SDKs, console, and docs.
background: Multiple teams have implemented adjacent hosted endpoints with slightly different input fields, streaming semantics, and error codes. This has caused inconsistencies in SDK behavior, customer confusion during migrations, and flaky tests in downstream integrations. We need an explicit contract and acceptance matrix that covers: input validation, streaming behavior, stable error surface, token semantics for cost reporting, and minimum telemetry for observability.
problem_statement: Without a crisp contract and acceptance criteria we observe: 1) breaking client behavior across SDKs when runtime optimizations change; 2) downstream customers miscomputing cost because of inconsistent token counting semantics; 3) ops escalations from unclear retry/error guidance; 4) uncertain rollout conditions that delay GA. This PRD reduces those risks by standardizing the contract and delineating the launch gate.
goals:
- Define canonical request/response schemas for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints.
- Specify streaming, truncation, and kv-cache hints so SDKs and runtimes behave consistently.
- Produce an acceptance matrix with measurable criteria (functional + nonfunctional) for QA/eng to verify.
- Provide an operations-ready rollout plan with monitoring and rollback thresholds.
- Ensure docs, SDKs, and console reflect the contract before GA.
out_of_scope:
- Deep model architecture decisions (quantization, kernel selection) except where they affect visible API behavior.
- Dedicated / Private infra-specific network controls (VPC-only behavior remains documented separately).
- New advanced features (tool-calling, complex function outputs) beyond structured output v1; those will be handled in follow-ups.
assumptions:
- Runtime will support streaming token delta events and final response markers.
- Token accounting library will be the single source of truth for all surface billing.
- SDK teams will accept minor ergonomics changes if they align with the contract.
- Backwards incompatible changes will be avoided; where unavoidable, will follow migration plan below.
success_metrics:
- Functional: 100% of contract test cases pass on staging for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank.
- Reliability: P95 end-to-end latency for typical chat prompt (<= 450ms for short prompts up to 128 input tokens) on hosted tier.
- Cost: Observed per-token accounting matches billing library within 0.1% on synthetic workload.
- Adoption: SDKs updated and released (JS/Python/Go) with contract conformance before GA.
- Post-launch: < 5 customer escalations related to API contract in the first 30 days.
user_stories:
- As an application developer, I can call the chat endpoint with messages list and receive a streaming delta, final 'done' event, and deterministic token count header.
- As a data scientist, I can request embeddings and receive a stable float32 array with length matching documented dimensionality and a reproducible normalization.
- As an SRE, I can observe per-route latency, per-token rate, and error breakdowns to trigger rollbacks when thresholds breach.
- As an SDK maintainer, I can rely on consistent error codes and typed response bodies to simplify retries and offline caching.
functional_requirements:
1) Input schemas: chat({messages: [{role, content, name?}], model, temperature?, max_tokens?, top_p?, stream?}), completions({prompt, model, temperature?, max_tokens?, stream?}), embeddings({input, model, batch_id?}), rerank({query, candidates[], model, top_k?}) - all documented.
2) Streaming: When stream=true, runtime must send an initial 'stream_start' event, a sequence of token-deltas or partial candidates, and a final 'stream_end' event containing metadata (token_count, duration_ms, model_version).
3) Token accounting header: Responses (streamed or single) must include X-Token-Count and X-Billing-Model headers. SDKs should not re-calculate token costs.
4) Error semantics: Stable error codes (400, 401, 403, 429, 500, 502, 503) with structured error payload: {code, message, retriable: true|false, retry_after?}.
5) Deterministic embeddings: Embedding outputs must be normalized to unit length if model spec says so; dimension must match model registry entry.
6) Backward compatibility: Existing customers with minimal field usage must continue to receive responses without additional required fields. Any new required fields must be behind opt-in params.
7) Observability: Each request must emit trace_id, model_version, route, latency_ms, token_count to our telemetry pipeline.
8) Contract versioning: Expose header X-Contract-Version with semantic version; GA must be v1.
nonfunctional_requirements:
- Availability: 99.9% for hosted tier during business hours.
- Latency SLOs: P95 <= 450ms for short chat prompts (<=128 tokens), P95 <= 1200ms for medium (129-512 tokens).
- Rate limits: Per-customer default rate limits documented; 429 must surface proper Retry-After.
- Security: All endpoints require auth; tokens validated and audited.
- Scale: Bulk embeddings calls must support batch sizes up to 1024 inputs with graceful degradation (queueing + 503 with Retry-After).
- Telemetry retention: critical per-request traces kept for 30 days for launch; extended retention is an addon.
acceptance_criteria:
- Contract conformance tests: engineering provides a test suite covering 120+ contract permutations (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) that pass in staging.
- SDK conformance: JS, Python, and Go SDKs consume streaming responses and surface token headers; each SDK has integration tests that pass against staging.
- Performance: Synthetic benchmark target: P95 latency targets met across 3 replica sizes on hosted capacity for representative workloads.
- Observability: Console routes surface per-route latency and per-token cost; sample trace links open to distributed tracing UI.
- Documentation: API reference, migration guide, example quickstart snippets, and acceptance matrix are published in docs site and linked from Console.
- Security: Security review completed and findings closed or mitigated; penetration test signoff for GA.
- Rollout gating: Canary region run for 72 hours with <1% error budget burn; otherwise rollback required.
- Backward-compatibility: No automatic breaking changes for requests that omit optional fields; opt-in toggles for new behavior validated.
acceptance_matrix:
A) Functional tests: pass/fail list per-endpoint (chat: 42 tests, completions: 32, embeddings: 28, rerank: 18).
B) Behavioral invariants: token header present, stream start/end emitted, consistent error codes.
C) Performance: P95 thresholds measured on standard synthetic suite.
D) Observability: dashboard panels created and show synthetic traffic metrics.
E) SDKs: all integration tests green.
F) Security: security issues <= 2 low/medium and no criticals.
Each row in the matrix must be signed off by product, engineering, and QA before promoting to GA.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge contract changes to runtime main with feature flag 'contract-v1'.
2) Deploy to staging and run full contract test suite.
3) Enable SDK integration tests against staging.
4) Canary rollout to us-east-1 at 5% traffic for 24h, ramp to 20% if no regressions.
5) Monitor error budget, latency, and token accounting signals; hold or rollback on thresholds.
6) Cross-region rollouts with incremental traffic increases and post-mortem if anomalies observed.
7) GA only after all contract tests, SDK releases, docs, and security signoff are complete.
launch_checklist:
- [ ] Contract test suite merged and passing in CI.
- [ ] JS/Python/Go SDK releases available and integration tested.
- [ ] API reference updated with schema and streaming examples.
- [ ] Console: route-level charts and token-cost panels live.
- [ ] Billing: token accounting library configured and validated with finance.
- [ ] Security review completed with signoff.
- [ ] Runbook created: steps to identify contract regressions and automated rollback.
- [ ] Canary run completed and post-canary review documented.
- [ ] Support playbook and escalation contacts published.
- [ ] Customer migration guide and changelog published.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Alerts: high 5xx rate (>0.5% sustained), token-count divergence (>0.5% from billing library), latency burn (>error budget thresholds).
- Dashboards: per-route P50/P95/P99, errors by code, token-cost per request distribution, SDK integration success rate.
- Runbooks: automated rollback trigger when canary error budget burned > 75% within 24h.
- SLO objective owners: runtime team and platform SRE.
migration_and_backward_compat:
- Provide a migration guide for customers who rely on earlier streaming behavior.
- Contract v1 will be opt-in via header X-Contract-Version until GA; clients default to legacy behavior.
- Deprecation schedule: announce 90-day notice before disabling legacy behavior; provide telemetry to identify affected customers.
- SDKs to support both behaviours for the deprecation window.

open_questions_and_decisions:
- Q1: Should embeddings be normalized by default or exposed as a parameter? Decision: default to model-registered behavior; expose explicit parameter 'normalize' if needed.
- Q2: Do we include token-snapshot events mid-stream for long-running streaming calls? Decision pending: product/eng to decide by 2026-03-20.
- Q3: What is the canonical schema for rerank candidates metadata? Decision: include candidate_id and payload but keep max payload size at 1KB.
engineering_notes:
- ENG must provide a contract-test runner that can be used by SDKS and QA.
- Streaming semantics must use standardized chunk envelopes (type: start|delta|end).
- Token-count header must be derived from the same tokenizer used for billing to avoid drift.
- Ensure runtime emits model_version and model_variant in all responses for reproducibility.
qa_plan:
- QA to run the canonical contract suite with synthetic and recorded user prompts.
- End-to-end tests: run SDK integration tests against staging cluster nightly.
- Performance: run load tests against canary deployment and validate P95/P99 budgets.
- Edge cases: payloads at size limits, malformed JSON, authentication failures, and retry semantics.
- Regression: maintain a matrix of previous incidents to verify fixes do not reintroduce regressions.
post_launch_followups:
- 7-day postmortem to review early customer issues and identify contract edge cases.
- 30-day metrics review: latency, errors, token-accuracy, support escalations.
- Follow-up items: structured output v2, function-calling contract alignment, and extended telemetry retention proposal.
- Customer outreach: compile list of customers using legacy behavior and offer migration assistance.
notes: This PRD is intended to be living; any contract changes after GA must follow the change-control process documented in the runbook and include migration tooling where feasible. The acceptance matrix will be maintained as a single table in the contract-tests repo and referenced by CI jobs.
